detail:
Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) Faces a $1.2 Trillion AI Spending Question: Will the Investment Pay Off?
Attiya Zainib
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:22 PM MST 3 min read
AMZN
^GSPC

Moon Capital Management an investment management company, recently released its Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here. The letter reported that its equity portfolio gained approximately 4% during the first nine months of 2026, compared with an approximately 12% year-to-date return for the S&P 500. The firm noted that market gains remained narrow, with nearly half of S&P 500 constituents declining during the period and the median stock gaining only about 4%. Much of the letter focused on AI investment, as major technology companies are expected to spend approximately $1.2 trillion on capital expenditures in 2027 and another $1.4 trillion in 2028. Although the semiconductor industry has benefited from strong demand, with the S&P Global Semiconductor Index rising approximately 95% through September, Moon Capital questioned whether the enormous infrastructure investments would generate adequate returns. The firm has avoided direct AI investments because it remains uncertain which companies will ultimately capture the economic benefits. The firm remains focused on businesses whose economics it can assess with confidence and whose shares trade at meaningful discounts to estimated intrinsic value. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

In its third-quarter 2026 investor letter, Moon Capital Management highlighted stocks like Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is a global technology and e-commerce company operating online and physical retail stores, advertising services, subscription offerings, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). The one-month return of Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) was 1.7% while its shares traded between $198.79 and $284.02 over the last 52 weeks. On November 9th, 2026, Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) stock closed at approximately $266.93 per share, with a market capitalization of $2.93 trillion.

Moon Capital Management stated the following regarding Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"The major hyperscalers (including Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)) are now expected to collectively spend approximately $1.2 trillion on capital expenditures in 2027 and another $1.4 trillion in 2028. By some estimates, AI-related investment accounts for roughly 30% of U.S. GDP growth and nearly half of S&P 500 earnings growth this year. The scale of the investment is extraordinary, but whether the eventual returns will justify the capital committed remains to be seen (Click Here To Read The Letter In Detail)."

detail:

SenesTech Reports Record Q3 2026 Revenue with 59% Year-Over-Year Growth
SenesTech

SNES
AMZN
Trade AMZN on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
SenesTech

Revenue increased 42% sequentially as e-commerce and subscriptions expanded;

Gross profit reached a record $796,000

SURPRISE, Ariz., Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SenesTech, Inc. (NASDAQ: SNES), an innovator in rodent control, today announced financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Q3 2026 Financial Highlights

Total revenue increased 42% sequentially to a record $1.097 million in Q3 2026, compared to $770,000 in Q2 2026, and increased 59% compared to $690,000 in Q3 2025. This was the second consecutive quarterly revenue record and the first quarter above $1 million, consistent with the preliminary revenue of approximately $1.1 million announced on October 15, 2026.

E-commerce revenue increased 52% sequentially and 337% year over year, representing approximately 71% of total Q3 revenue.

Subscription revenue increased 53% sequentially and 234% year over year. Combined subscribers across Amazon and the Company's website increased 72% compared to Q2 2026, strengthening the recurring revenue base.

Direct B2B revenue increased 19% sequentially and 2% year over year. Sequential growth was driven by process changes to the Company's B2B efforts, which drove growth in the pest management, government and commercial verticals.

Evolve® revenue increased 67% year over year to $979,000 and represented 89% of product revenue. ContraPest® revenue increased 13% year over year to $118,000, driven by higher refill sales.

Gross profit increased 40% to a record $796,000 in Q3 2026, compared to $567,000 in Q2 2026, and increased 84% compared to $433,000 in Q3 2025.

Gross margin was 72.6% in Q3 2026, compared to 73.6% in Q2 2026 and 62.8% in Q3 2025.

Net loss for Q3 2026 was $2.0 million, compared to $1.8 million in Q2 2026 and $1.3 million in Q3 2025.

Adjusted EBITDA loss was $1.4 million in Q3 2026, compared to $1.4 million in Q2 2026 and $1.1 million in Q3 2025.

Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter were $4.0 million. Subsequent to the end of the quarter, the Company raised $1.2 million in gross proceeds from the ATM.

Net cash used in operating activities declined each quarter in 2026, falling to $1.3 million in Q3 from $1.7 million in Q2 2026 and $1.9 million in Q1 2026.

Recent Operational and Strategic Highlights

Amazon Revenue and Subscriptions Continue to Grow: Amazon revenue increased each month of Q3, bringing in new customers and expanding the recurring subscription base.

B2B Sales Team Expanded: The Company added two salespeople, bringing the team under Executive Vice President of Sales Jack Karabees to four, with two additional hires expected by year end. The team is focused on building repeat business across targeted domestic verticals.

E-commerce Reach Expanded Through Grove Collaborative: SenesTech added Grove Collaborative as a third-party e-commerce channel, bringing Evolve® to an engaged base of consumers focused on sustainability.

Assessment and Monitoring Services Launched for B2B Customers: In July, SenesTech began offering assessment services to help B2B customers measure rodent activity and understand the scope of an infestation. Customers can choose an assessment performed by SenesTech or deploy the Company's tracking products themselves, with results analyzed using SenesTech's internally developed AI tool. These services complement existing implementation and deployment services and are expected to provide an additional revenue opportunity.

Municipal Results Support Broader Adoption: Chicago's Wicker Park Bucktown program, which incorporated SenesTech's assessment services and Evolve® into an integrated pest management approach, reduced average rat activity intensity by 88% over 12 months. Evolve has expanded to six Chicago-area Special Service Areas and wards. In Swampscott, Massachusetts, Evolve Rat, combined with sanitation and waste management improvements, helped reduce measured rodent activity by 43% over six months.

Sandstrom Partners Engaged to Support Branding and Marketing: SenesTech engaged Sandstrom Partners, a Portland, Oregon, brand development firm whose clients have included Nike, Target and Coca-Cola, as a strategic advisor on marketing and branding. An early priority is helping retain Amazon customers and attract new customers by more clearly communicating how the Company's rodent birth control products work.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) shares rose about 1.5% in Tuesday trading after its Ring unit unveiled an indoor security drone and a business patrol robot, expanding the company's push into the smart home and commercial security market.

The Ring Drone Cam, priced at $250, can fly between rooms and investigate when alarms trigger. It offers about eight minutes of flight time before returning to a charging dock. Ring CEO Jamie Siminoff said the device may act as a crime deterrent.

title: Billionaire David Rubenstein Passed On Facebook’s $30K Startup Pitch, Sold Amazon Before Billions In Gains. 'I Didn’t Take It Seriously'
detail:
Billionaire David Rubenstein Passed On Facebook’s $30K Startup Pitch, Sold Amazon Before Billions In Gains. 'I Didn’t Take It Seriously'
Image via Shutterstock
Casey B. Renner
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:14 AM MST 6 min read
AMZN
CG
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

A billionaire investor's biggest regrets go back to the early days of the internet.

Carlyle Group (NASDAQ:CG) co-founder David Rubenstein passed on a chance to invest in Facebook. At the time, founder Mark Zuckerberg was trying to raise $30,000 to launch the site.

"I didn't take it seriously," he told Business Insider in September.

Rubenstein and his partners also sold their stake in Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN). He said the shares would have been worth billions if they'd held on.

Saverin Kept A Piece Of Facebook

Rubenstein said on the "Earn Your Leisure" podcast last month that he heard about Facebook from Evan Rachlin, one of Zuckerberg's Harvard classmates. 

Rachlin, who later became Rubenstein's son-in-law, told him the site would help students at Harvard find dates. Rubenstein had seen dating services come and go and didn't think Facebook would last. 

Another Harvard student, Eduardo Saverin, helped fund the launch. He left the company in 2005 and later settled a dispute over his stake. Saverin still owned shares when Facebook went public in 2012. 

Saverin co-founded venture capital firm B Capital in 2015. He's now based in Singapore, where he backs startups as the firm's co-CEO. Forbes says most of his wealth still comes from his shares in Facebook parent company Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META).

Trending: Warren Buffett once said, "If you don't find a way to make money while you sleep, you will work until you die." Here's how you can earn passive income with just $100.

A Book Catalog Led To A 1% Stake

In Amazon's early days, Jeff Bezos offered book distributor Baker & Taylor a stake in the company for access to its catalog of books in print. Carlyle held a majority stake in the distributor, which has since shut down. 

Jeff Bezos offered Baker & Taylor a stake in Amazon for access to its catalog of books in print. Baker & Taylor turned down the shares and agreed to let Bezos use the catalog for five years at $100,000 a year, Rubenstein said on "Earn Your Leisure." 

When Rubenstein heard about the deal, he flew to Seattle to see if the original offer was still on the table. Bezos told him that two years had passed since the original offer and that he no longer needed Carlyle's help as much. He ended up with about 1% of Amazon.

title: Uber Joins with Amazon on Food Delivery: A Major Growth Catalyst?
detail:
Uber Joins with Amazon on Food Delivery: A Major Growth Catalyst?
Maharathi Basu
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:10 AM MST 3 min read
UBER
AMZN
BBY
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Uber Technologies UBER and Amazon AMZN have partnered to introduce a new restaurant delivery benefit for U.S. Amazon Prime members. Under the arrangement, eligible members can enjoy zero delivery fees on restaurant orders of $25 or more placed directly through Amazon.com or the Amazon Shopping app, with deliveries fulfilled by Uber Eats. The service requires neither a separate Uber account nor an additional app.

The benefit is available to all Prime subscribers, including those enrolled in the discounted Prime for Young Adults and Prime Access programs. By integrating Uber Eats into its platform, Amazon aims to enhance the convenience and value of Prime membership while expanding access to restaurant delivery services.

The partnership provides Prime members across nearly 10,000 U.S. cities and towns access to hundreds of thousands of restaurants through Uber Eats' extensive delivery network. Coverage spans major metropolitan markets, suburban neighborhoods and rural communities, offering a broad selection of national chains, regional restaurants and local establishments.

Participating restaurants include prominent brands such as Wingstop, Chipotle and Sweetgreen, alongside regional favorites and independent dining establishments. Beyond waived delivery fees, members can access exclusive promotional offers through Amazon, potentially generating annual savings exceeding $175.

To encourage adoption, eligible Prime members can receive $20 off each of their first two Uber Eats orders of at least $25 during the initial 14-day promotional period. Additionally, Prime Visa cardholders can earn 5% back on Uber Eats purchases through Dec. 5, 2026, subject to applicable eligibility requirements.

The ordering process is integrated into Amazon's existing shopping experience. Members can access the service through Amazon's dedicated Uber Eats webpage or shopping application, browse nearby restaurants and complete purchases using their existing Amazon credentials and payment methods. Following order placement, Amazon provides delivery updates through email and push notifications, while Uber Eats issues the final confirmation.

The collaboration is expected to strengthen Amazon's Prime ecosystem by combining restaurant delivery with its established retail, grocery and entertainment offerings. Members can also access free Same-Day Delivery on eligible perishable grocery purchases exceeding $25 through Amazon Grocery.

The expanded restaurant delivery offering complements existing Prime benefits, including fast shipping, Prime Video, Amazon Music, cloud gaming, digital reading services and Alexa+ capabilities. Subscribers also receive access to select ultrafast delivery services, Amazon Pharmacy benefits, healthcare savings and fuel discounts at participating stations.
